1.explanation: FormField.js is responsible for wrapping inputs and applying the pad prop around their container. Because it pads the content box, any child that assumes 100% width will overflow. RangeInput.js and its StyledRangeInput.js define the slider’s layout and default to full width without accounting for container padding. Adjusting StyledRangeInput (e.g. adding box-sizing: border-box or making width responsive) or enabling RangeInput to accept a boxed width will prevent the overflow and recenter the thumb inside the padded FormField.
1.bug_scenario: When embedding a <RangeInput> inside a padded <FormField>, the slider’s track and thumb extend beyond the field’s content boundary and the thumb is no longer centered in the gray inset. In other words, FormField applies padding around the input, but RangeInput’s underlying styled component still renders at full width (100%), which overflows the padded container and makes the thumb appear off-center.

2.explanation: The RangeInput components control the CSS for the native <input type="range" /> including width and box-sizing. In StyledRangeInput.js the track is set to width: 100% without box-sizing: border-box, so when FormField adds padding (in FormField.js) the input actually overflows its container. RangeInput.js wraps and positions the styled input. Adjusting the box-sizing on the range input or changing how FormField applies padding will prevent the overflow and re-center the thumb within the FormField.
2.bug_scenario: When a RangeInput is placed inside a FormField with pad enabled, its track extends past the padded content area and the thumb is no longer centered in the FormField. In the screenshot you can see the green and black range track overflowing the light-grey FormField border and the circular thumb is off-center horizontally — the input’s width is calculated as 100% of the padded container’s content box, causing overflow.
